1 (PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE MAULIK J.SHELAT)

1. The present appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the MV Act') by the insurance company challenging judgment and award dated 18.11.2017 passed in Motor Accident Claim Petition (MACP) No.1491 of 2008 by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (MACT), Rajkot.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition (MACP) No.1491 of 2008
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/690/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 2.

The short facts of the case appears to be as under :
2.1

On 20.09.2008 at about 6:00 pm deceased was riding his motorcycle near Thorala Police Station area of Gondal and passing through Aaji Bridge and at that time driver of the truck bearing registration No. GJ 11 X 8668 dashed his truck with motorcycle.
Thereby, deceased has sustained injuries and succumbed to it.

The claimants, who are legal heirs of deceased have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to be paid by the driver,
owner and insurance company of the truck.
2.2 Opponent No.1 - owner of the truck though served chosen not to appear before the tribunal.
Opponent No.2 has filed its written statement at Exh.16 opposing the averments made by the claimants in their claim petition.
After appreciating the evidence on record and hearing submission of the parties the tribunal has decided the issue of negligence by holding him solely negligent for causing accident.

So far as quantum of compensation is concerned after appreciating NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/690/2018 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/12/2024 undefined evidence lead by the claimants tribunal has awarded in all a sum of Rs.14,81,000/-.
2.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with impugned judgment and award the present appeal has been filed by the opponent NO.2 insurance company.

3. Submissions of the appellant:
3.1

Learned advocate Mr. Krutik Parikh appearing for the appellant insurance company would submit that the tribunal has committed an error by considering 50% future prospective income of deceased which is contrary to the principle laiddown in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 (13) Scale 12 as the deceased was engaged as daily wager earning Rs.6000/- per month.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 (13) Scale 12
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3.2 He would submit that considering the nature of employment and the status of the deceased in employment with Jyoti CNC Auto Private Limited at best 40% instead of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/690/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 50% future rise of income to be considered.
So, according to him tribunal has awarded more than just compensation.
4. Submissions of respondents 4.1
Per contra learned advocate Mr. Hemal Shah would submit that it is true that deceased was engaged as daily wager in Jyoti CNC Auto Pvt. Ltd.

But his pay slip and the New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mona W/O Bikas Singh Vishnusing on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34401121/
2 certificate on record would indicate that he would engage on permanent basis.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mona W/O Bikas Singh Vishnusing
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would further submit that there is no error committed by the tribunal while considering 50% futur rise of income.
4.2 He would further submit that under conventional heads, lesser amount has been awarded to the claimants.
According to him tribunal has granted just and reasonable compensation and considering benevolent provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, this Court may not disturb the same.
4.3 Heard learned advocates appearing for the parties.
No other and further arguments have been made.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/690/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined

5. Point for consideration:
5.1
Whether in the facts and circumstances of the case any error is committed by the tribunal while granting compensation?

6. Findings of the Court:
6.1 After going through impugned judgment, the record and proceedings and hearing respective learned advocates appearing for the parties we are of the view that if the tribunal could have considered 40% rise of the income considering the status of the deceased being daily wager then at the same time, we cannot loose site tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,30,000/- for loss of consortium, Rs.5000/- as funeral expenses and Rs.5000/- towards loss of estate, which is on lower side.
6.2

So, keeping all these facts in mind even if we recalculate and the compensation as per the submission of learned advocate for the insurance company, there is hardly any NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/690/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined difference in the compensation so awarded by the tribunal, which does not requires interference by this Court.

Thus,
in view of the aforesaid considering the megare difference, amounting to Rs.41,500/-, we would not like to disturb the award at the instance of insurance company.

7. Conclusion:
7.1 In view of aforesaid discussion and observations this Court would not like to interfere with the impugned judgment and award.

In view of the dismissal of the appeal FDR shall be released in favour of the original claimants through RTGS /
NEFT.
Hence appeal is dismissed no order as to costs.

(BIREN VAISHNAV, J) (MAULIK J.SHELAT,J) DRASHTI New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mona W/O Bikas Singh Vishnusing on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34401121/
